newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB say to start merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB say to start merger talks.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG and regional bank Norddeutsche Landesbank said on Wednesday they planned to begin talks on a long-expected merger.

The two banks, which received approval last year from their state owners to start talks aimed at intensifying co-operation, said Bankgesellschaft Berlin, Germany's sixth largest commercial bank, would lead the merged unit.
The talks should be completed by the end of the year and the new company could start operations by mid-1998.
The banks also said the new bank would be based in both Berlin and Hanover. It would be partly owned by regional state authorities and partly held in private hands.
A merger between the two banks has long been viewed as one of the most likely consolidation steps in an industry bogged down by excess capacity.

Bankgesellschaft is in the throes of an overhaul which will include shedding 10 percent of its 17,00 staff in 1997 and 1998 and closing branch offices after reporting a 90 percent slump in 1996 net profit.
News of the merger boosted Bankgesellschaft shares, sending them to a new 12-month high of 37.95 marks, a gain of 47 pfennigs or 1.2 percent. The 30-share blue-chip DAX index was up 0.5 percent.
